status: CLOSED. All four PRs open, none merged, none deployed. Three of four CI states are as good as they can be before a merge; the fourth is red for two reasons that are both measured and neither of which this lane introduced.
missionPremise: The largest conformance finding on the sellable SmartCity product line, axe `color-contrast` at wcag2aa, fails on `.badge` and `.p-quiet.pill`. Those are kit classes coloured by `--sc-*` tokens declared in `web/sc-kit.css`, and that file is byte-identical across `smartcity-dashboards`, `smart-files` and `plan-review` with its own header stating that a repo which edits a token value has forked the system. The finding therefore CANNOT be fixed in a Dashboards PR: it is a product-line change that has to land as identical bytes in three repos with a kit re-vendor behind it. Source: OPS-17 amendment A-080, taken 2026-08-19 on the operator's ruling 'okay lets fix the kit then', which approved contrast remediation as a product-line change and set the conformance target at BOTH WCAG 2.0 AA (Revised 508) and WCAG 2.1 AA (ADA Title II). The governing design ruling is `_decisions/2026-08-17_smartcity_product_line_design_system.md` (one Empressa kit governs Dashboards, Smart Files, Plan Review and future Asset Management) and `_decisions/2026-08-17_smartcity_visual_law.md` (quiet surfaces, loud exceptions, honest absence; light is first-class).
completionPredicate: A stranger can evaluate this without me by doing five things. (1) `git ls-tree <branch> web/sc-kit.css` in all three product repos and `vendor/sc-kit.css` in the kit returns ONE blob hash, `8113df901f77c86ca034ca95060b7cc1f57e96ee`. (2) Serving the dashboards branch locally and running `P:/tmp/g94-scan/contrastscan.mjs` reports `color-contrast` at 0 nodes in BOTH themes across the 16 surfaces, where it reported 54 dark and 643 light before. (3) `git diff main..g94/contrast-tokens -- web/sc-kit.css` in each product repo shows exactly six changed lines, all of them token VALUES, no token added or renamed, no rule and no selector touched, and `web/index.html` and `web/shell.css` untouched. (4) Every ratio quoted travels with its counting rule. (5) The two CI reds on the kit PR are reproducible on a pristine `main` worktree, proving they are inherited rather than caused.
scopeBasis: The boundaries are drawn where the measurement stops being about a token value. IN: the four `--sc-*` value declarations that every failing node resolves to, in all three product repos plus the kit's vendored copy, and the one kit gate whose pinned delta a value change necessarily moves. OUT, deliberately and each for a named reason. (a) `web/index.html` and `web/shell.css` in every repo: G-95 owns them in `P:/tmp/g95-dash` and a second lane editing them is a merge conflict by construction. (b) `scrollable-region-focusable` (4 nodes) and `heading-order` (11 nodes), and the 2.4.2 `document.title` finding: they are G-95's plan rows and are unchanged before and after here. (c) Re-vendoring the kit's `index.html`/`app.js`: refreshing them pulls G-93's nav-foot markup, which puts a second source segment inside one `.prov` and requires the `Prov` component to accept two sources. That is a component-contract change and a different card; absorbing it would make a contrast PR unreviewable as what it is. (d) Reconciling `30b_smartcity_design_system.md` section 4.1, which still declares the old token values: editing a canonical doc is planner-owned. (e) Adding a cross-repo byte-identity check: it is a NEW control, and DEV_PROCESS 5.4 says propose rather than unilaterally remediate. (f) A contrast gate in CI: same reason, and it is closer to G-95's gate row than to this one. (g) Any scan of the smart-files or plan-review surfaces themselves: those repos received identical bytes because the token block is identical, not because their surfaces were measured; no claim is made about their node counts and the PRs say so.

prs.ciConclusionString: NONE. This repo has no .github directory, no workflow, and no test script in package.json, so the PR has ZERO check runs. This is not a passing state and must not be read as one: there is nothing to read a conclusion string from. Reported as a finding below.

prs.ciFailureIsExpectedAndExplained: run 32294040694, exactly one failing test, `arm B: vendored copies byte-match the live upstream checkout`, raw: `vendor/sc-kit.css has drifted from empressaioemail-tech/smartcity-dashboards/web/sc-kit.css. Upstream is canonical; run npm run refresh:vendor.` The kit's CI checks smartcity-dashboards out at `ref: main`, not at a PR head, so the refreshed copy is compared against an upstream that has not merged. It clears when dashboards PR #30 merges. A SECOND, independent arm-B failure on `vendor/index.html` sits behind it and does not clear on that merge; see findings.

byteIdentityCheck.countingRule: git ls-tree <ref> <path>, i.e. git's blob sha1 over the checked-in bytes; checkout-independent and unaffected by autocrlf, which matters because these clones are on Windows

before.verdict: IDENTICAL in all four, and equal to the hash the dispatch named. The system had not forked, so this was the right card.

after.method: the bytes were not re-derived per repo. `git show HEAD:web/sc-kit.css` from the dashboards branch was piped into the other two working trees and staged, so identity is a property of the procedure, not of three careful edits.

whatAssertsTheCrossRepoIdentity.answer: NOTHING ASSERTS IT across the three product repos. One of three edges is checked, and it is checked in one direction only.
measured: smart-files: the only reference to sc-kit.css anywhere outside the file is the <link> tag at web/index.html:24. Its CI (.github/workflows/test.yml: Unit, HTTP round trip) never reads the file.

plan-review: NO .github directory, no workflow, no test script. Its only mentions are the <link> tag at web/index.html:7 and a prose comment at web/styles.css:1, 'Tokens come from sc-kit.css. No local token fork.' A comment is not a control.

smartcity-dashboards: src/first-paint.test.mjs, src/ui.test.mjs and src/shape.test.mjs read web/sc-kit.css and assert only its INTERNAL properties. The 'byte-identical across three repos' claim appears solely in comments (first-paint.test.mjs:680, shell-parity.test.mjs:80) and in the file's own header.
doc_repo: no script and no catalog entry references sc-kit at all.

smartcity-kit: test/vendor-parity.test.mjs is the ONLY real control. Arm A pins vendor/sc-kit.css by sha256; arm B byte-compares it against a smartcity-dashboards checkout, and ci.yml checks that repo out and then greps the log to fail if arm B skipped, so it cannot silently not-run. It asserts kit against dashboards. It says nothing about smart-files or plan-review, in either direction.
whatAssertsTheCrossRepoIdentity.consequence: The product line's stated invariant is enforced on one of three edges. smart-files and plan-review could drift from dashboards indefinitely and every CI in the program would stay green. This is DEV_PROCESS rule 0's shape exactly: the control that exists is the header comment, and a comment depends on someone remembering.
whatAssertsTheCrossRepoIdentity.recommendation: One card, not three: a single check that compares the three product copies against each other, owned by whichever repo has CI, plus CI for plan-review, which currently has none at all. Not done here because a new control is a new card and DEV_PROCESS 5.4 says propose rather than remediate.

changedTokens.countingRule: ratios are WCAG 2.x sRGB relative luminance, (Llighter+0.05)/(Ldarker+0.05), truncated to 2dp so a printed 4.57 is never a rounded-up 4.495. 'worst' means the lowest ratio against ANY background the token lands on across 16 surfaces in that theme, measured with P:/tmp/g94-scan/tokenprobe.mjs. Every failing node was normal-weight text at 12 to 15px, so 4.5:1 applies to all of them and the 3:1 large-text and non-text allowance to none.
changedTokens.whySix: the light block declares the two tokens once each; the dark palette is declared TWICE in the file, once under @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) and once under :root[data-theme=dark], .sc-dark, and both had to move or the media-query path and the explicit-toggle path would disagree
changedTokens.method: hue and saturation held EXACTLY (208.2 / 13.6% light, 208.0 / 12.8% dark); only lightness moved, light 49.0% to 39.5% and dark 54.1% to 57.6%
changedTokens.notChanged: --sc-quiet-wash deliberately not moved: it is a separate token and it is one of the measured backgrounds, so moving it would change what the fix is measured against. No token added, renamed or removed. No rule, no selector, no type ramp, no geometry, no spacing, no duration.

axeRerun.instrument: P:/tmp/g94-scan/contrastscan.mjs, the same 16 targets and the same axe build (P:/tmp/VPAT/axe.min.js) as P:/tmp/g82v/.ds-sync/_axescan.mjs, extended to keep axe's per-node color-contrast data and to drive the real theme lever
axeRerun.countingRule: NODES = DOM elements failing a rule, summed across the 16 surfaces within one theme; the same element on two surfaces counts twice, because a surface is the unit a conformance report is written against
axeRerun.target: local server from the g94-dash clone, PORT=8791, cross-origin requests aborted so the run is hermetic and bounded. NOT the serving revision: this measures the branch, and per the standing decision CODE-DONE is not CUSTOMER-DONE. The 54 reproduces A-080's figure exactly, which is what ties the local baseline to the serving one.

findings.title: The A-080 color-contrast baseline of 54 nodes is DARK ONLY. The real baseline was 697.
findings.measured: dark 54, light 643, both over the same 16 surfaces with the same axe build.
findings.cause: the theme lever on this product is data-theme on <html>, resolved at first paint from localStorage key 'theme' (web/index.html:36 THEME_KEY, :115 root.setAttribute), and web/index.html:2 ships data-theme="dark" statically. Emulating prefers-color-scheme does not move this palette. A scan that sets Playwright's colorScheme therefore reads the dark surface twice and looks like two-theme coverage. Verified directly: an unpatched colorScheme run returned an identical 54 for light and dark, pair for pair, including identical per-pair node counts.
findings.instrumentFix: the scanner now seeds localStorage and then ASSERTS document.documentElement's data-theme equals the requested theme after load, throwing if it does not, so an unapplied theme can never be reported as a scanned theme. This is the DEV_PROCESS 2.2 shape: a gating indicator proven able to fire.
findings.bearing: light is first-class per the visual law. Sizing this fix on 54 would have tuned a value to dark and left 92% of the defect standing. It also means any other conformance figure taken by that scanner against this product is dark-only until re-run.
findings.carriedTo: G-95, which owns the CI conformance gate: the gate must drive data-theme, not prefers-color-scheme, or it will pass a light-theme regression.

findings.title: Nothing asserts the cross-repo byte-identity the design system depends on.
findings.detail: see whatAssertsTheCrossRepoIdentity above. One of three edges checked, one-directional.
findings.recommendation: one card: a check comparing the three product copies against each other, plus CI for plan-review.

findings.title: plan-review has NO CI at all, so its PR has zero check runs and nothing can be merged on a conclusion string.
findings.measured: no .github directory in the repo; package.json has no test script; `gh pr view 3` returns an empty statusCheckRollup.
findings.why it matters: the merge rule is 'merge only on the conclusion string SUCCESS'. On this repo there is no string. An absent check and a passing check must not look the same, and here they do. Merging PR #3 is a judgement call the planner has to make knowingly, not a gate that passed.

findings.title: smartcity-kit main is ALREADY RED against smartcity-dashboards main, and nothing can see it.
findings.measured: on a pristine `main` worktree of the kit, run against a `main` worktree of dashboards, arm B fails: `vendor/index.html has drifted from empressaioemail-tech/smartcity-dashboards/web/index.html`. Timeline: dashboards merged G-92 (#27, #28) and G-93 (#29) at 17:49 to 17:58Z on 2026-08-19; the kit's last CI run was 16:58Z with conclusion `success`; nothing re-runs the kit on an upstream event.
findings.structure: the upstream-drift guardrail only fires on a KIT event. It cannot see upstream move until someone touches the kit repo. This is the same failure the kit's own README narrates at the 139-to-143 vocabulary move, recurring one hour later, which makes it a pattern rather than an incident.
findings.notAbsorbedHere: refreshing vendor/index.html pulls G-93's nav-foot markup, which puts a second source segment inside one .prov and requires the Prov component to accept two sources. That is a component-contract change and a different card. vendor/index.html and vendor/app.js keep their existing pins; the manifest records per-file provenance, which is what its per-file shape is for.
findings.recommendation: two things, one card. Re-vendor index.html/app.js and widen Prov to the two-source form. Separately, a scheduled or upstream-triggered kit CI run, because a drift check that only runs on its own repo's events is a control that depends on someone remembering to touch the repo.

findings.title: The product and the canonical design doc now disagree on four token values.
findings.detail: doc_repo 30b_smartcity_design_system.md and .html section 4.1 still declare --sc-ink-3 #6C7E8E / #7B8B99 and --sc-quiet #6C7E8E / #7B8B99. The kit's gate 1c pins the delta between the product's token block and that doc extract; it was one line (the Compass spring constants, finding F-1) and is now seven added and six dropped.
findings.handling: the gate was widened in BOTH directions as EXACT line arrays, not filters, so a new divergence still turns it red; `npm run prove:gates` confirms the gate 1c injection still fires (34 of 34 injected violations caught and named, 1 of 1 legitimate-payload control green). The kit's copy of the doc extract was NOT hand-edited, because that would make the kit assert a doc_repo state doc_repo does not have.
findings.owed: planner-owned edit to 30b section 4.1 in both .md and .html, after which the kit re-vendors the extract and gate 1c narrows back to one line.

findings.title: There is no contrast check anywhere in the product line.
findings.measured: grep for 'contrast' across src/ and web/ in smartcity-dashboards returns zero files. The type ramp has a machine gate (src/type-conformance.test.mjs enforces the 12px floor); colour has none.
findings.bearing: this fix is a point-in-time correction. Nothing stops the next token edit from reintroducing it. G-95 owns the axe-in-CI row and this is an argument for its priority.

findings.title: Design cost of the fix, stated rather than hidden.
findings.detail: --sc-ink-2 must stay louder than --sc-ink-3. On #FFFFFF light, ink-2 is 7.33 and ink-3 moved from 4.18 to 5.91, so the separation narrowed from 3.15 to 1.42. On #12191F dark, ink-2 is 8.15 and ink-3 moved from 5.06 to 5.69, separation 3.09 to 2.46. The quiet tier is still a visible step below body ink in both themes, but the light hierarchy is materially tighter than it was. That is the unavoidable price of a 4.5:1 floor against --sc-doc-ground #DDE3E8, and the alternative (moving the ground tokens instead) would have changed the map and document canvases, which is a larger visual move than this card was scoped for.

findings.title: The Git Bash job pid did not map to the Windows node process, exactly as the dispatch warned.
findings.detail: the detached server recorded pid 3202924 in bash; the actual Windows process was 67924, found by CommandLine match through Win32_Process. The kill was verified by probing the port (http_code=000, connection refused) rather than by the absence of a process, because a pid that never mapped cannot prove anything by being gone.
